newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hypo-Bank sacks management at fund unit.
newsitem.headline: Hypo-Bank sacks management at fund unit.

text.p: Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG said on Monday it would replace the management of its loss-making unit H.C.M. Hypo Capital Management in a restructuring following a 1995 tax probe.
The current two-man management board, made up of Bryant Boyd and Heinrich Morgen, would be replaced "as soon as possible," a Hypo-Bank spokesman said.
H.C.M. doubled its loss to about 18 million marks last year and suffered heavy fund withdrawals due to a probe into alleged tax evasion in which its offices across Germany were searched.
The investigation was part of a wider probe at a number of German banks which have been accused of helping customers to evade tax, a charge the banks have consistently denied.
Hypo-Bank said in a brief statement it would maintain H.C.M. as an independent asset manager.
Earlier on Monday Hypo-Bank chief executive Eberhard Martini denied rumours that all H.C.M's branches would be closed but did not rule out that some may be shut down.
"We are in the process of restructuring H.C.M. so that it can be successful," Martini told journalists.
H.C.M. has said it does not expect to return to profit before 1997. Its assets under management have plunged to 1.3 billion marks from the level of 2.5 billion before the tax affair.
The Hypo-Bank statement said the bank had for a long time not been satisfied with the subsidiary's cost management.

German newsletter Platow-Brief had on Monday reported that H.C.M. would close all branches in 14 days and that Hypo-Bank had been in talks to sell H.C.M. to Citibank but that the price had been too high.
Talks with two other potential buyers had also foundered, Platow Brief said.
H.C.M. was set up in 1989, has 10 branches and 152 employees.
